parallel.requirements: Recognized the ESM .mjs output hierarchy, no external npm dependencies, local imports, manual --a parsing, Python print/repr parity, and black-box executable probing requirements.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Parent probed behavior, then delegated strutils, pyrepr, dictutils, argparse, and test17 entrypoint to five children, while the parent retained final integration and verification responsibility.
parallel.implementation: Children wrote the five files. The parent later inspected strutils and test17, changed under2camel back to the classic boltons rule, changed the entrypoint to parseArgs(process.argv), and adjusted slugify after diff failures.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent joined child outputs from the shared /output tree, edited integrated files after handoff, listed the final file tree, and delivered test17.mjs plus four lib modules.
parallel.verification: The parent ran executable comparisons on representative inputs, checked argparse exit codes, and confirmed twelve output cases and basic error paths, but did not match the serial run's later all-delimiter and randomized fuzz depth.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation still failed 2 of 161 cases. The visible process leaves a repaired but initially incompatible parseArgs entrypoint contract and a simpler final edge-case record than serial.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same ESM .mjs, local import, manual argv parsing, black-box behavior, repr formatting, FrozenDict order, and output parity requirements.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One actor owned discovery, implementation, integration, testing, and delivery without delegation, so component interfaces were resolved inside the same local context.
serial.implementation: The serial actor implemented pyrepr, strutils, dictutils, argparse, and test17, then iteratively refined slugify delimiter handling, empty/all-delimiter cases, argparse -- handling, and Unicode titlecase behavior.
serial.integration_and_delivery: All modules were written and edited by the same actor, with the final tree containing test17.mjs and the four required lib modules in /output.
serial.verification: The serial actor ran many executable comparisons, including hand-picked edge cases, argparse stderr/exit checks, control-character inputs, and a normalized 60-case randomized fuzz pass.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation still failed 2 of 161 cases despite broad visible local testing, so any remaining defect is not isolated by the visible trajectory.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel captured the prompt's ESM, .mjs, no dependency, argv, repr, and behavior-matching obligations before delegation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used the same prompt and treated the migration as a full black-box behavior reproduction task.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Requirement coverage was broadly similar, but serial derived more edge-case requirements from probing before closure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposed into five child-owned files, with the parent responsible for final join and repairs after receiving handoffs.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept all discovery, coding, integration, and verification in one actor's context.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced cross-component ownership boundaries; serial avoided those boundaries but did less concurrent production.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel specified module scopes but omitted the parseArgs call signature from the entrypoint child's interface context, producing a flagged mismatch.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial implemented parser and entrypoint together, so the parseArgs interface stayed local and coherent.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The concrete interface difference is the parallel entry child guessed a definition-style parseArgs call and the parent had to change it to process.argv.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children created separate modules, then parent corrected under2camel, parseArgs usage, and slugify after comparison failures.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial built the same module set directly and iteratively refined tricky behaviors such as slugify delimiter handling and argparse quirks.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial's implementation path included more direct black-box refinement; parallel depended on component handoffs plus parent patching.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: All five child results returned; the parent inspected key returned warnings and took over necessary repairs before final delivery.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child-result lifecycle because one actor owned all work through completion.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel incurred join and handoff handling, but no completed child result was left unjoined or trapped.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Children wrote distinct assigned files in the shared /output tree, and the parent repaired integrated source after handoff.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote the same final file set without concurrent writes or child-owned artifacts.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had shared-tree coordination but no proven live same-file collision or overwrite; the material issue was an interface mismatch, not a write race.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran representative executable diffs, detected one slugify mismatch, fixed it, then confirmed twelve cases and matching exit codes.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran repeated targeted probes, a full battery after fixes, argparse checks, and a 60-case randomized fuzz pass normalized for program name.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial verification was visibly broader, but both official evaluations later failed the same two hidden samples.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel completed within budget after 1708 agent seconds and retained 689 seconds of cell budget.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed within budget after 1416 agent seconds and retained 981 seconds of cell budget.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel used more wall-clock agent time and tool calls, but neither run timed out and both reached completed closure.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The authoritative completed status records show both solutions failed, each passing 159 of 161 official tests. The runs differ in process rather than official outcome: serial performed a single-owner deep black-box implementation and fuzz pass, while parallel used five child-owned components and then parent-side reconciliation of integration defects. The retained parallel pattern explains a real coordination cost, not a score split.
parallel_contributors: Five-way delegation produced the required files and enabled component work, but the entrypoint/parser interface needed parent repair after handoff.
Parallel verification caught and fixed representative output mismatches but was narrower than the serial edge-case/fuzz campaign.
serial_contributors: Single-owner implementation kept parser and entrypoint contracts in one context.
Serial verification covered more delimiter, Unicode, control-character, argparse, and randomized cases before closure.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both runs still missed two hidden official cases, and the visible logs do not isolate those misses to a parallel-only coordination event.
The serial implementation appears more detailed around slugify edge cases, but the official pass counts are identical.
evaluator_effects: The official evaluator establishes the both-fail relation and identical 159/161 score; it does not identify the hidden failing cases in the mounted evidence.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained pattern is an adverse parallel process episode only

The parent owned integration after child handoff, read the integrated files, edited incompatibilities, and ran whole-program comparisons.
The entrypoint and final /output file tree were assigned and produced; assembly was not ownerless.
The parent managed the end-to-end transition from probing through delegation, repair, verification, and final response.
The parent probed behavior before delegation, but the run still launched productive child implementation and no mandatory gate caused unfinished work.
Investigation preceded child work, but implementation was not deferred until it became incomplete or insufficiently verified because of that phase boundary.
No indispensable implementation or integration path was starved; the parent repaired the critical integration issues before closure.
Five children and high token use are visible, but the run did not exhaust the budget or close because fan-out consumed the remaining time.
Each child had a bounded module or entrypoint assignment; no single overbroad child scope left indispensable work unfinished.
The retained issue is an omitted cross-component call contract, not a standalone task, environment, acceptance, or delivery requirement missing from a child brief.

candidates.near_match_reason: The missing fact governed interoperability between two separately owned components, so the interface-contract label is more specific than a general incomplete task brief.

candidates.reason: All five subagents completed and returned handoffs; no active child was explicitly stopped before needed work finalized.
A complete promotable candidate was not left unpromoted at deadline; the final files were present and artifact validation succeeded.
The parent ran post-repair comparisons after integrating changes, so no child result was merged only after the relevant verification without a follow-up check.
Every delegated implementation was available in /output and the parent inspected, edited, or included the resulting files before delivery.
No verifier child produced a concrete finding that remained trapped below the parent; verification was parent-run after child handoffs.
Where child outputs were defective or ambiguous, the parent took over and edited the affected integrated files before closure.
The parent consumed completed child results, including flagged issues, and acted on them rather than proceeding inconsistently without inspection.
The parent did not wait until timeout or a hard deadline without inspection; it received results, edited files, and ran checks.
The separate files had expected component boundaries; no competing cross-file design claimed overlapping behavior in a way that required reconciliation beyond the retained interface contract.
No two live agents edited the same source or configuration file and observed or reconciled a concurrent same-file change.
Parent edits to completed child files were integration repairs, not one live agent wholesale replacing another live agent's non-entry source ownership.
The parent edited the entry deliverable after the entrypoint child completed; no concurrent actor replaced a deliverable while another owned or used it.
There was no broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion replacing multiple current outputs and invalidating another actor's final-tree work.
Although child agents wrote to the shared /output workspace, they had distinct file assignments and no unstable-state or provenance problem beyond the retained interface mismatch.
A child testing against a sibling module in /output was intended module integration and did not contaminate probing or verification with an unstable auxiliary artifact.

retained_patterns.reason: The parser and entrypoint were delegated separately without giving the entrypoint child the concrete parseArgs(argv) contract. The child reported the ambiguity and used a wrong call shape, and the parent repaired test17.mjs before integrated verification.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: The parent spent an extra integration cycle reading and editing the entrypoint to replace the incompatible child-chosen call convention.
retained_patterns.near_match_reason: The omitted fact was specifically the interface between two child-owned components, not an independent task requirement for one child.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: The parseArgs repair was not also counted as Missing Implementation Join, No Failure Takeover, Deliverable Overwrite, or Unused Completed Result because the parent received the result and corrected the interface mismatch.
The strutils slugify and under2camel fixes were treated as implementation refinement from child output, not separate concurrency labels, because the parent verified and repaired them before closure.
cardinality_audit.underlabel_check: All 13 Level-2 rows and all 32 Level-3 candidates were audited; only the parseArgs cross-agent contract omission clears the retention gate.
cardinality_audit.overlabel_check: No downstream timeout, join, write, or monitoring label was added for the same repair chain; the retained label has its own anchors and consequence.
